research_question: Can an initially two-anchor rigid F37 fibre remain continuously engaged during the known Stage26a conditioning transient and recover a persistent two-anchor terminal state without damaging the qualified 216-grain sand packing?
claim_boundary: Fixed-fibre dry-mechanical prefilter only. It does not qualify free fibre motion, polymer properties, permeability, migration, deformation, flow, or hydro-mechanical coupling.

rationale.diagnosis: The Revision-1 ten-block rule incorrectly required two contacts at every conditioning block. The accepted Stage26a positive control had one persistent declared anchor during blocks 1-25 and 32-33, then two declared anchors throughout blocks 34-60 and passed its subsequent free-relaxation qualification.
rationale.anti_tuning_boundary: The redesign uses only the frozen positive and negative controls. Revision-3 candidate01 has not been run in YADE and contributes no data to this gate.
rationale.mechanical_interpretation: One anchor during early servo equilibration is treated as transient engagement, not isolation. Promotion requires continuous engagement and a sustained two-anchor terminal window.

control_acceptance.positive_stage26a: Insertion has exactly two contacts, the temporal contact gate passes, and terminal sand-health gates pass.
control_acceptance.negative_stage26b_failure: Insertion has exactly two contacts per fibre and at least one fibre becomes isolated in the transient or terminal window; this known failure must reproduce.

frozen_unchanged: fibre F37 geometry, mass, density, stiffness, friction, and fixed kinematics
100 Pa isotropic target stress, gravity, damping, timestep safety, controller rate
insertion geometry and exact two-contact insertion condition
terminal sand-health, penetration, fibre-fibre, and intraclump gates
execution_order: revision3_candidate01 only after both controls reproduce
